```{python}
import polars as pl 
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
import polars.selectors as cs
# add the additional libraries you need to import for ML here

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

data_url = "https://byuidatascience.github.io/DS250-Course-Polars/Data/StarWars_with_emails.csv"
```

<!-- The first 10 rows are not part of the datset we need.

The columns headers are split across two rows. We need to clean and simplify the column headers-->

```{python}
# Read in and tidy up the first row
a = pl.Series(pl.read_csv(data_url, skip_rows = 10, n_rows=1, has_header=False, encoding = 'utf8-lossy').row(0))
# Note the non-aschii character in the column "Do you consider yourself to be a fan of the Expanded Universe". (column AF if you open it in Excel). 

# BTW: Detecting what it is and where can be difficult

# Lossy means that invalid utf8 values are replaced with � characters. When using other encodings than utf8 or utf8-lossy, the input is first decoded in memory with python. Defaults to utf8...ignore_errors = True does not replace the non-utf8 character with a blank space like you would hope

a[2] = "seen_any" #simply overwrite the value at index 2

# Rather than changing each column header manually,
# here we use regex to apply changes more efficiently
a = (
  a.str.replace(r".+seen.+", "seen_")
   .str.replace(r".+rank.+", "rank_")
   .str.replace(r"(.+favorably.+)", "fav_")
   .fill_null(strategy = "forward")

   .str.replace("\uFFFD+", "") #this gets rid of the question marks in a diamond characters 
   .str.strip_chars()
   .str.to_lowercase()
   .str.replace_all(" ", "_")
   .str.replace(r"location(.+)", "location")

)
a[3] = "star_wars_fan"
a[30] = "who_shot_first"
a[31] = "know_expanded_universe"
a[32] = "expanded_universe_fan"
a[33] = "star_trek_fan"
```

<!-- Combine series q and a into one series to be used as column names-->

```{python}
b = pl.Series(pl.read_csv(data_url, skip_rows = 11, n_rows=1, has_header=False, encoding = 'utf8-lossy').row(0))

b = (
  b.str.replace(r"Star Wars: (Episode \w+) .+", "${1}")
   .str.replace("Response", "")
   .str.replace_all(" ", "_")
   .fill_null("")
   .str.strip_chars()
)

```

```{python}
#Now combine the two series, each of which contains part of the desired column header
new_names = (a + b).to_list()

# Read in the data, skipping over the column header rows
# and use 'new_names' as the column headers
df = pl.read_csv(data_url, skip_rows=12, has_header=False, new_columns = new_names )
```


1. __Remake the respondent names from the email column. Show the first 5 rows of the result. Each respondentID has a unique email they used to submit their survey. We can see that each of the emails have a different format for their names.__

__Use regex to create a first name column, a last name column, and a email domain column to your data set for each row. Show the first 5 rows of the result (you don’t have to show all the columns, just the email, first name, last name, and email domain).__

__This table should be placed either in the the Methods section or an Appendix of the report submitted for this unit (see below).__

```{python}
df_name_domain = df.with_columns(pl.col("email")
.str.strip_chars()
.str.splitn("@", 2).struct.rename_fields(["email_string","domain"])).unnest("email")

df_categorized = df_name_domain.with_columns(periods = pl.when(pl.col("email_string").str.contains(r"\.")).then(pl.col("email_string")).otherwise(None), others = pl.when(pl.col("email_string").str.contains(r"\.")).then(None).otherwise(pl.col("email_string")))

df_last_first = df_categorized.filter(pl.col("others").str.contains(" ")).with_columns(last_name = pl.col("others").str.extract(r"(^\S+)\s"), first_name = pl.col("others").str.extract(r"/s(/S+)$"))

df_first_last = df_categorized.with_columns(
  first_name = pl.when(pl.col("periods").is_not_null())
  .then(pl.col("periods").str.extract(r"^([a-zA-Z]+)"))
  .otherwise(pl.col("others").str.extract(r"([a-zA-Z]+)$")), 
  last_name = pl.when(pl.col("periods").is_not_null())
  .then(pl.col("periods").str.extract(r"([a-zA-Z]+)$"))
  .otherwise(pl.col("others").str.extract(r"^([a-zA-Z]+)")),
  domain = pl.col("domain").str.to_lowercase(),
  email=(pl.col("email_string") + "@" + pl.col("domain").str.to_lowercase())
).select(["email","first_name","last_name","domain"])
```

2. __Make a table that counts the number of times each domain is used. Note that sometimes the email domain is not lowercase. Make them uniform for clean counting.__

__This table should be placed either in the the Methods section or an Appendix of the report submitted for this unit (see below).__

```{python}
df_domain_counts = df_first_last.group_by("domain").agg(count = pl.col('domain').count())
```
